title: Skrzypiec 2013 lumbar disc segment (articular joints removed) anterior shear strength (peak load) under 500 N compression

quantity.name: anterior shear strength (peak load)
quantity.definition: anterior shear strength (peak load); linear fit 0-150 N of 2nd cycle (strength = peak anterior load in overload)

source.authors: Skrzypiec DM, Bishop NE, Klein A, Puschel K, Morlock MM, Huber G
source.sample: 12 cadaveric lumbar segments from 11 male spines: 6 motion segments (MS, L2-L3) and 6 disc segments with articular joints removed/damaged (DS, mostly L4-L5); disc grade II-III

protocol.summary: Segments potted (up to 2/3 of vertebral body), Ringer solution at 37 C, 30 min; 500 N axial compression via dead weights for 15 min (preconditioning) and maintained; X-Y table decouples axial/shear; 2 shear cycles at 50 N/s 0 -> +200 N anterior -> -200 N posterior -> 0; then anterior shear overload at 0.5 mm/s to 15 mm. Stiffness = linear regression of 2nd cycle, 0-150 N (anterior) and 0 to -150 N (posterior). Peak load = shear strength.
how_to_simulate: Fix the lower vertebra; apply 500 N axial compression (follower-free dead weight) and let creep 15 min
Apply anterior/posterior shear force of the upper vertebra to +-200 N at 50 N/s; then anterior displacement 0.5 mm/s to failure
Report shear stiffness (0-150 N slope) and peak shear load

extraction.check_notes: Table 1 from text layer (digital PDF). Median row as printed. Note LUM-06 contributed both an MS (L2-L3) and a DS (L4-L5). doi not printed.

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (or inside [min, max] when no SD)
